identifiableFields.description:
If both objects being compared are {@link Identifiable} and either isA the other, normally only the `id` field
is used to determine equality. If this flag is set, the exact type and all fields of the instances are compared
in this case as well.

dontAllowOverride.description:
If true, throw an error if a value in the merged object already exists in the original object. Otherwise the
value in the merged object overrides the one in the original object.

For Obj values, this applies to each field. For arrays, this applies to each element that is itself equal.
For Maps, this applies to each key. For all collections, empty collections are treated as null (not specified).

convert.description:
If true, attempt to convert fields to the correct value type and throw an error if conversion fails. Otherwise,
an error will be thrown if the values are not isCoercible (assignment compatible). Conversion is potentially
expensive so this is off by default.

references.description:
Control the merging of references (inner Obj values), both as individual values and collection elements.
 - `REPLACE` indicates the object is replaced wholesale (other object wins).
 - `MERGE` indicates fields are merged individually.

If you want objects to win as-is, use `REPLACE` (the default):
```
merge({ id: '1a2b' }, { name: 'Jack' }) -> { name: 'Jack' }
```

If you want merging of corresponding fields in the object, use `MERGE`:
```
merge({ id: '1a2b' }, { name: 'Jack' }, MERGE) -> { id: '1a2b', name: 'Jack' }
```

collections.description:
Control the merging of inner array, sets and maps (nested collections).
 - `REPLACE` indicates the collection is replaced wholesale (other collection wins).
 - `CONCAT` indicates the elements in the other collection are added after the original values.
   For maps and sets acts like `MERGE`.
 - `MERGE` indicates collection elements are merged individually by key. For arrays, the key is the index
   and for maps the key is the map key. Sets are merged by value.

If you want non-empty collections to win as-is, use `REPLACE` (the default):
```
merge([1], [2]) -> [2]
```

If you want all members of both collections in the result, use `CONCAT`:
```
merge([1], [2], CONCAT) -> [1, 2]
```

If you want merging of corresponding (by key) values in the collection, use `MERGE`:
```
merge([1], [2], MERGE) -> [2]
merge([{ id: '1a2b' }], [{ name: 'Jack' }], MERGE) -> [{ id: '1a2b', name: 'Jack' }]
```

Note that the last example assumes ValuesEqualSpec#useId is true as well (matching Identifiable objects by id).
And the last two examples with Objs assume #references = `MERGE`.

title:
This spec is the optional argument used to control the behavior when merging values.
